S Stagecraft AI

The planner that keeps your summit on track

AI agents read your inbox, flag what's slipping, and re-plan the day in 30 seconds. You approve every change.

Kalab Dagem · MGT 409 AI Foundations for Managers · Fall 2026
https://github.com/Kalab-yale/mgt409-final-stagecraft

The problem

A 350-person summit, run by volunteers, out of Gmail and a spreadsheet

15+
deadlines, 8 vendor and sponsor contracts, dietary counts for 362 people, speakers from 3 cities
14
emails in one inbox that change the plan or need a reply, plus one fake invoice carrying a hidden AI instruction
~45 min
to re-plan one day-of problem by hand: a free room that fits, AV, conflicts, messages (estimate)

Example: the student team behind the Yale Black Venture Summit. One or two big events a year, organized by people with full-time jobs or classes. When something slips, it costs fees, penalties, and goodwill.

What's new

Not another event suite, and not a chatbot

TodayThe gap
Cvent, Bizzabo (enterprise suites, adding AI copilots)Built and priced for event companies (Bizzabo reported at ~$18k/yr); don't read your inbox
Asana, Sheets, NotionDon't know room capacity, catering cutoffs, or locked keynotes
ChatGPTHolds no event state, can invent a room, follows instructions hidden in a pasted email
  • Your inbox becomes plan changes: facts, red flags, drafted edits, replies
  • Verified day-of fixes: AI proposes, code guarantees capacity, no double-booking, and the keynote stays put
  • You stay in charge: agents only draft; nothing saves or sends without your click
  • About $0.50 per event per month in AI (estimate)
How the agents work

13 agents, 3 safety layers, 1 human approval

gpt-6-luna for every agent (course key). Typed outputs between agents; the hard parts (room search, constraint checks) are code.

Safety

Three layers, each proven by a test

1 · Injection firewallHidden instructions blocked before any AI reads them: 0 tokens
2 · Action lockCode rejects made-up rooms, overfull rooms, double-booking, keynote moves
3 · Spending limit60k tokens, $0.15, 4 steps per run; stops loops

Attack test: 3 of 3 stopped. 39 incidents logged
